quarterly_data.signal: GlobalWafers completed pricing of its global depositary share (GDS) offering on September 22, 2026, raising gross proceeds of 14.32億美元 (US$1.432 billion; about NT$454億, i.e. NT$45.4 billion). It issued 5,000萬 (50 million) GDS units, each representing one common share, to be listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and traded on its Euro MTF market, at US$28.64 per GDS (about NT$908.32 per share), a discount of about 6.46% to that day's closing price of NT$971 (the stock rose 4.3% that day). Proceeds will fund raw-material purchases in foreign currency and investments in overseas subsidiaries, the latter mainly for capacity expansion. The company says the offering was fully subscribed in a short time with demand about 4 times the deal size, and that it is the third-largest Taiwan overseas depositary receipt issuance ever; it follows a US$6.89億 (US$689 million) GDS completed in March 2024. J.P. Morgan Securities plc was sole global coordinator and sole bookrunner.
quarterly_data.figure: 14.32億美元 raised (~NT$454億); 5,000萬 GDS at US$28.64; ~6.46% discount; ~4x subscribed

quarterly_data.signal: In the GDS release GlobalWafers says its existing 12-inch capacity is fully loaded and 8-inch utilization remains high, with customer demand clear and visibility continuing to improve. It says the semiconductor recovery has broadened from AI and HPC to more end markets: AI logic-chip and memory capacity are expanding together, driving demand for niche wafers for advanced nodes and specialty applications, while industrial, automotive, communications and consumer markets are gradually recovering. It cites long-term wafer demand growth from AI, HPC, high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, thermal solutions and silicon photonics, and customers' growing preference for local-for-local sourcing.

GlobalWafers says its global expansion (described as the largest in its history, across the U.S., Europe and Asia) is entering the harvest phase: the new Texas (U.S.) fab has passed qualification at several Tier-1 customers and its output keeps increasing, and key customers have raised demand visibility for the Texas fab through long-term agreements and strategic funding support (customers not named); output of newly expanded 12-inch SOI wafers at the Missouri (U.S.) site has risen significantly; the Niigata (Japan) plant set a quarterly revenue record in the second quarter of this year and is expected to set another record in the third quarter; the Utsunomiya plant has repeatedly set shipment records. The company cites its U.S.-based 12-inch advanced silicon wafer and SOI wafer mass-production capability as a competitive advantage.
quarterly_data.figure: Texas fab passed several Tier-1 customer qualifications; Missouri 12-inch SOI output significantly up; Niigata quarterly revenue record
